notes: strand: strandOf(world, reader) answers {narrative, event, location, character, now, same}; the world carries its elements as the owner is served them, the ids its hidden mark keeps (hidden), and its readers, exactly as the lens and charter fixtures do. Each filled slot is {id, type, name}, type the kind the slot holds (now holds a location); an empty slot is null.

readers: a reader's rung is owner (the whole world), contributor (the world less the hidden), guest (exactly the whole and known_of ids it lists; a known_of id is a stub: its id, type and name, its description and its dates, no link and no extension field; hidden beats known_of) or public (the world less the hidden and the room elements, and nothing at all unless the world carries open: true), as the lens and charter fixtures define them. The strand reader resolves every slot through that one view and keeps no second copy of the rule.

the key: the fixture gives x_strand as stored; the server's rule 1 (no key served when the named Narrative is out of the reader's view) is keel's test, not the reader's. A reader handed a key it cannot resolve answers an empty strand.

mark: the value is an object whose narrative member is a string id; event and location are each a string id, null or absent (null and absent read as unset); any other shape (a bare string, any of the three members the empty string, narrative missing or not a string, event or location a number or an object) reads as no mark: every slot null, same null. No reader trims a member: one of white space alone (a space, a tab, an ideographic space) is a string that names no element, so its slot is null, and so is an id with white space on it; a non-empty narrative that names nothing (spaces alone among them) is a mark that leaves every slot null. A reader needs no id-format test: an id that names no element in the view is an empty slot; the doctor names the shape.
stub: a narrative the reader knows only as a stub fills the narrative slot ({id, type, name}) and nothing else, since a stub serves no events and no protagonist.
order: the reading never depends on a multi-link's order; the event must be IN the narrative's events and the location IN the event's locations, position ignored.
no fallback: character comes from protagonist only, never from the event's characters; location from the mark only, never from the character's location; now from the character's location only.
same: true when now and location are both set and the same id; false when both set and different; null when either is null.

kind: a slot holds only its own kind, an element's type compared to it trimmed and folded as the room profile defines it; an id of another kind in the mark or in a parent's list leaves the slot empty. same compares ids, never names.

shapes: a multi-link that is not a list reads as empty (a bare string in events or locations puts nothing in the list); a filled slot's name is the element's name as served, an empty string when it has none, never null.
compare: objects are compared as values; the order of keys carries no meaning, so a reader that writes {type, id} or {id, type, name} in another order answers the same.
